title: When the Rivergate Wakes
premise: Lior Montrose has spent a decade outrunning her mother's legacy, digging for hire and vanishing before anyone learns her name. When the Rivergate floods recede and expose a chest bearing the seal of Vessany—a nation erased from every map—she recognizes her mother's private mark burned into the lid. The chest holds proof that the expedition that killed her mother found something worth killing for again, and the people funding Lior's own dig want it silenced. To bring her crew home alive, she must lead them out through collapsing river country while deciding whether to destroy the inheritance that explains everything—or claim it.
about_author: Marguerite Zhou is a former field surveyor who spent six seasons mapping floodplains across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose skills keep them alive but never let them rest.

chapters.title: Silt Season
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Working a contract dig on the Rivergate floodplain, Lior reads the soil better than her employers and plans to leave before the pay dispute turns ugly. When the river drops after the floods, it exposes a sealed chest in an impossible place. Beat: restless competence curdling into dread as she recognizes the craftsmanship of someone she buried years ago.

chapters.title: The Seal of Vessany
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone at dawn, she opens the chest: documents, a survey journal in her mother's hand, and a bronze seal from a country that officially never existed. Her employer Halvard arrives too soon, sees too much, and offers to triple her fee if she says nothing. Beat: the past stops being avoidable; grief and suspicion arrive together.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lior and Tam, her foreman, who notices the chest and starts asking quiet questions. Lior lies badly and covers it with work, assigning night watches she doesn't explain. A stranger arrives claiming to be a hydrologist sent by the funding consortium. Beat: paranoia takes root inside a team that was already fraying.

chapters.title: What the Journal Says
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, intercut with her mother's journal entries. She learns the original expedition found the Vessany archive beneath the riverbed—and that her mother chose to bury it rather than report it, knowing what the funders would do. The 'hydrologist' is caught photographing their site. Beat: Lior realizes she is living her mother's last choice in reverse.

chapters.title: Halvard's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Halvard privately calculates losses he can justify: equipment, yes; people, if necessary. He cuts the radio line and blames the storm season. Tam, loyal to Lior but not blind, confronts her and gets half the truth. Beat: the expedition becomes a trap with a countdown—the river will rise again within days.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She decides to move the whole crew out early through the old survey route from her mother's journal, telling them it's a safety call. The hydrologist sabotages a boat; they lose supplies crossing the channel at night. One crew member, Ivet, nearly drowns and is saved by the stranger—who then defects to their side. Beat: survival forces honesty; the lie becomes shared burden.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with Tam. The route passes the submerged entrance her mother described, exposed by the same low water. Inside: the Vessany record of a deliberate erasure—an entire nation disappeared by treaty, its archive hidden by the last archivist. Lior understands why her mother died protecting it. Beat: inheritance reframed—not property, but responsibility.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Halvard's men close in as the river begins to rise. A running fight through the flooded cut; the defected stranger is wounded covering the retreat. Lior must choose between the chest's contents and a crew member's life, and chooses without hesitation—but Halvard retrieves the dropped satchel of copies. Beat: the price of survival made literal and paid gladly.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. Cornered on the rising levee, Lior bargains with Halvard using the one thing he fears: publicity. She reveals she mailed the journal's testimony to three newspapers before leaving camp. Halvard's leverage collapses as the flood destroys the site itself, burying the archive forever under moving water. Beat: memory wins not by being kept, but by being told.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, weeks later. The crew is home; the story runs; Halvard's consortium unravels quietly. Lior keeps only her mother's seal and burns nothing else, because the truth now lives outside her. For the first time she unpacks her bags in a town with a river she likes. Beat: resolution—she stops moving, having finally inherited something worth staying for.
